newsitem.title: IVORY COAST: Strike hits Christmas air travel in West Africa.
newsitem.headline: Strike hits Christmas air travel in West Africa.

text.p: A strike by African air traffic controllers grounded flights at airports across much of West Africa on Wednesday, disrupting travel on Christmas Day, airport officials said.
Officials said the stoppage had been called off at Abidjan airport, the hub of air travel in the region, but flights there were still grounded by action elsewhere.
"There are still no departures and we are asking people to call back later for information," an airport duty official told Reuters, confirming that Abidjan controllers were back at work.
French radio reported that Air France had cancelled Christmas Day flights to Abidjan and about half a dozen other West African destinations -- Bangui, Libreville, Cotonou, Lagos, Dakar and Douala.
Airport officials said only one plane landed at Abidjan by 11.45 a.m. (1145 GMT) -- an Air Afrique flight which left Lome, Togo, despite the strike action there.
Reports from neighbouring states said flights were also disrupted in the Burkina Faso capital, Ouagadougou, the Senegalese capital, Dakar, and Niamey, Niger.
Air traffic controllers in 15 African countries belonging to the Agency for the Safety of Aerial Navigation (ASECNA) launched a 48-hour strike over pay and conditions at dawn on Wednesday.
But union leaders at ASECNA's headquarters in Ouagadougou have since said the stoppage would be indefinite following the suspension of their leader by the agency's authorities.
"We regret to announce that the radio blackout order will henceforth be observed for an indefinite period until our demands are satisfactorily addressed," said a union statement.
Union president Alexandre Damiba said the stoppage was being observed in all member countries.
Just about all 15 ASECNA member states are former French colonies in West and Central Africa and the Indian Ocean.
